concepts.name: Integer multiplication algorithms
concepts.gloss: The grade-school O(n^2) method and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer O(n^1.585) method for multiplying n-digit integers.

concepts.name: Binary representation and bit strings
concepts.gloss: Nonnegative integers written as strings of 0/1 digits, or in other bases, with n-bit length.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers reduced modulo m, with indices taken cyclically.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Primes, greatest common divisors and pairwise coprime integers.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, residues modulo the product correspond bijectively to tuples of residues modulo each modulus.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The divide-and-conquer O(N log N) algorithm computing a length-N discrete Fourier transform using two-point butterflies.

concepts.name: Roots of unity
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers z with z^N=1, used as the evaluation points of a Fourier transform.

concepts.name: Linear algebra over a field
concepts.gloss: Vector spaces, linear maps and matrices, including invertibility, rank, subspaces and dimension.

concepts.name: The field F_2 and binary vector spaces
concepts.gloss: The two-element field where addition is XOR, and vector spaces F_2^h of bit vectors.

concepts.name: Triangular matrices and factorization
concepts.gloss: Matrices with zeros above or below the diagonal, and factoring a matrix into such factors.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: Bijections of a finite set, which rearrange the positions of a list.

concepts.name: Divide-and-conquer recurrences
concepts.gloss: Solving cost recurrences of the form T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n) by unrolling or the master theorem.

concepts.name: Logarithms and iterated logarithms
concepts.gloss: Base-2 logarithms and their growth rates compared with powers of n.

concepts.name: Little-o, Omega and liminf asymptotics
concepts.gloss: Standard asymptotic comparison notation and limits of ratios of functions.

concepts.name: Convolution of sequences
concepts.gloss: The sequence c_k=sum a_i b_{k-i}, which gives coefficients of a polynomial product.

concepts.name: Norms and error bounds
concepts.gloss: Vector norms, linear maps of norm at most one, and bounding accumulated numerical error.

concepts.name: Dyadic rationals and fixed-point numbers
concepts.gloss: Rationals with power-of-two denominators, with truncation and rounding to a fixed number of bits.

concepts.name: Gaussian function
concepts.gloss: The function exp(-x^2) and its basic properties.

concepts.name: Direct sum and tensor product of vector spaces
concepts.gloss: Product structures on vector spaces, used to view a list as a multidimensional array.

concepts.name: Polynomial evaluation and interpolation
concepts.gloss: Recovering a polynomial from its values at distinct points.

concepts.name: Asymptotic definition of algorithm cost and time complexity
concepts.gloss: Running time as a function of input length for deterministic algorithms.

background.summary: The reader has finished undergraduate computer science: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics, linear algebra over the reals and complex numbers, basic algebra (modular arithmetic, primes, finite fields of two elements at an introductory level), recurrences and divide-and-conquer algorithms such as Karatsuba and the FFT in outline. They have seen Turing machines and tapes but not tape-level complexity theory, and have not studied Fourier analysis on groups, coding theory, or the research literature on fast multiplication.
